summary: New box Infinitiv: example for sense 1b in Infinitiv (Jan 2.5/1460)

data.turoyo: Xori Brahim: Kmaḥwe bi dayro yaləf. Ḥur d umarnolox, u səryoyo mu xəboṭo yo. D mxabəṭ u nošo ba kṯowe, gədyoləf.
data.translation: Father Brahim: It seems he learned at the monastery. Look, I tell you, Syriac comes from working through things. When a person works through books, he will learn.

rationale: Supports and widens round 1 intellectual 1b; same quotation supplies the first Infinitiv and a thin Infectum cell. English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation.

summary: New sense 1b: fig. untersuchen, erforschen (Geschichte)
rationale: A historian investigates historical material to establish the age and nature of churches; the direct abstract object and knowledge goal distinguish this from physical rummaging. One attestation.

summary: New sense 2: sich bemühen, sich anstrengen (mit d-Satz)
rationale: Mxabatle d obe taz explicitly makes the doctoral-thesis action the goal of effort; this is clearer Turoyo evidence than the earlier free escape translation.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (63/73)

data.turoyo: <...> Mxabaṭli bi xaṣraṯe w paṯe, de bu zor mofaqli i damančayayḏi mu qəlfayḏi, maḥtoli b iḏoṯi, kit eba šwaʕ ḏ̣arbe. <...>
data.translation: Ich durchsuchte diese Körperseite und jene, brachte mit Mühe meine Pistole aus dem Futteral heraus und nahm sie in die Hand. Es waren sieben Schuß darin.

rationale: Thin Preterit cell; b-marked bodily search domain and an explicit purpose in context.

summary: example for sense 1b in Infectum (93/9)

data.turoyo: Annaqla kito ʕetoṯe ste hawxa ʕatiqe appe, faqat ḥa lo=koḏəʕ, heš m ayna zamane ne w mə=šəkəl ne. M u=sabab d noše b u=aṯrayḏan tarəġčiye layto, ḥatta d mxabəṭ at=tariġat w d mofaqqe w d oḏəʕ, mənne w mə=šəkəl ne.
data.translation: Es gibt unter ihnen auch gar alte Kirchen, aber man weiß nicht, aus welcher Zeit sie stammen und welcher Art sie sind; denn es gibt in unserer Heimat keine Historiker, von denen einer die Geschichte erforschen und herausbringen und feststellen könnte, was sie eigentlich sind und welcher Art sie sind.

rationale: Only attestation of the new figurative inquiry subsense; full causal sentence establishes the historian's task.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (103/34)

data.turoyo: Komər kul ḥa mxabaṭle ʕar ruḥe, mən hesənǧawo, kṯuwwe aʕle.
data.translation: Da suchte jeder bei sich herum, und wer immer ein Eisengerät hatte, schrieb das darauf.

rationale: Fifth Preterit example; explicit reflexive search domain with ʕal assimilated before r.

summary: example for sense 1b in Infectum (Jan 2.5/1461)

data.turoyo: Bi madrase kyoləf šmənto, mede normal. I naqqa d huwele kṯowe, d mxabəṭ, kyoləf səryoyo kayiso, d lo kfoyəš, falgo yo.
data.translation: At school he learns a little, something normal. When he has books and works through them, he learns Syriac well. Otherwise he remains half.

rationale: Second book-study context for the broadened round 1 intellectual subsense; conditional learning frame. English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation.

summary: example for sense 2 in Preterit (Jan 3.5/53)

data.turoyo: <...> Mxabatle, d obe taz d doktora bi falsafe du dino.
data.translation: <...> He strove to submit a doctoral thesis in the philosophy of religion.

rationale: First clear effort-plus-d-clause construction; one attestation, not based on etymology or the English alone. English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation.

summary: Sense 1b: revise the gloss
after: fig. untersuchen, erforschen; sich eingehend mit Büchern beschäftigen
rationale: Widen the round 1 historical-research subsense to explicit book study for language learning; the semantic change removes the history-only restriction, without another numbered sense.

summary: Physical search domains are marked by b- (63/73), ʕal/aʕl- (grave; 96/349), and reflexive ʕar ruḥe (103/34). The historical-research use instead has a zero-marked abstract object and is retained as one figurative subsense.

The duplicated finite verb at 67/18 marks continued activity, not two independent example contexts; 67/29 is already among the inherited references. The prison-flight paraphrase in German at Talay 1/190 does not establish an independent sense 'attempt'.
Talay 1/189 (= LB 189) gives human scrabbling compared with a mole. The finite relative and repeated 1sg predicate remain ordinary sense 1; do not count each repeated token as another quotation.
No light verb plus noun requires an idiom entry. The loan history listed in the head is retained without using comparative etymology to decide contextual senses.

Literal sites take ʕal, including ʕal u rišayḏa at Jan 2.23/4242; book study has ba kṯowe and an understood domain in the next verse. The direct/oblique alternation does not require separate intellectual senses.

New II.2 is justified by the Turoyo goal clause in Jan 3.5/53. Round 1 correctly treated the German attempted-escape paraphrase alone as insufficient; this new independent evidence changes the sense inventory without silently reassigning that older example.
mxabaṭte at Jan 2.23/4263 does not securely identify buyers as agents or a human object. The pressure/badgering reading is withheld; general effort remains possible.
Plain t in mxabatle/Mxabatle is retained as printed beside ṭ; no text normalization or new stem.
Preterit sense 1 already has four examples after round 1; Jan 2.23/4242 does not fill a remaining thin cell and is retained only as valency evidence.
What licenses ʕal before mxabəṭ in PrS 41/14? Confirm the source before using it as a model clause or changing the inherited government.
In 93/9, does at=tariġat denote written historical accounts specifically or history more broadly? The new gloss leaves that open.
At Jan 2.23/4263, identify agent and ending of mxabaṭte: human-target pressure or the owner’s efforts? Do not accept the machine English badgered him as decisive.
Does xəboṭo function as the II Infinitiv by the glossary convention or a lexical action noun? The semantic link to the immediately following finite mxabəṭ is clear.
Should the old xbṭ.II.t.preterit.2 attempted-escape quotation move to new sense 2 after checking its larger context? No original example is moved from this new evidence alone.
Correct English spelling: ful → full
rationale: The adjective full is misspelled in the phrase full of gold.

summary: The rummaged domain can be a body side, a grave, an animal or one's own possessions. Foraging without an overt object is a possible contextual extension, but PrS 41/14 has uncertain ʕal placement.
Book study to learn Syriac supports the round 1 intellectual-investigation proposal and broadens its original history restriction; Infinitiv xəboṭo and finite mxabəṭ occur together.
